United States → Vietnam

The Vietnam Relocation Guide

Every legal route from the USA to Vietnam, as one decision tree. Including the routes that do not exist.

Edition v1.0.0 Verified September 8, 2026 Next review December 8, 2026 8 pathways 23 cited sources

Read this before you rely on anything here. This is researched reference material, not legal or tax advice, and no lawyer-client relationship is created by buying it. Immigration rules change without notice and are applied with discretion by individual officers. Every claim is numbered to a source you can check yourself, and each source is labelled with how much weight it carries.

Everything here was verified on September 8, 2026. Before you spend money or book a flight, confirm the specific rule against the cited source or with a licensed Vietnamese immigration adviser. USD conversions in this guide assume approximately VND 26,000 = US$1. The rate moves. Treat every dollar figure as an order of magnitude, not a quote, and check the rate on the day you move money.

Start here: what is not true

Six beliefs that cost Americans the most money on the way to Vietnam. We lead with these because the expensive mistakes happen before anyone files a form.

Widely believedVietnam has a golden visa I can buy.

Actually: It does not, as of the verification date of this guide. A 5-to-10-year 'golden visa' was proposed to the Prime Minister by the Tourism Advisory Board in 2025 and has been widely reported as if it were live. There is no decree number and no application channel. Some sites cite a 'Resolution 41/2026/QH15' pilot; no Vietnamese government source confirms that resolution exists, and the outlets carrying the claim sell visa services. 1415

Why the myth persists: Golden-visa search traffic is extremely valuable to agencies. Reporting a proposal as a program generates leads years before any program exists.

Widely believedAmericans get 45 days visa-free like the Brits and the Europeans do.

Actually: No. Vietnam's unilateral visa exemption covers roughly two dozen countries. The United States is not one of them. Americans need a visa for every single entry, including a weekend trip. The practical default is the 90-day e-visa. 98

Why the myth persists: Blog posts written for a UK or EU audience get syndicated and rewritten without the nationality caveat.

Widely believedThere is a digital nomad visa, or a retirement visa.

Actually: Vietnam has neither. There is no visa category for a remote worker paid by a foreign company, and no category for a retiree living on passive income. The new UĐ1 tech visa is not a nomad visa: it runs through a Vietnamese employer, university, or research body, which excludes freelancers and remote employees of foreign firms. 161

Why the myth persists: Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines all launched nomad or retirement visas. Writers assume Vietnam followed. It did not.

Widely believedI'll just open a company and that gets me residency.

Actually: Only above a capital threshold. Contributing under VND 3 billion (roughly US$115,000) puts you in the DT4 tier, which grants a visa of up to 12 months and no temporary residence card. You will have a Vietnamese company, ongoing accounting and tax obligations, and still no residence card. The residence card starts at DT3, meaning VND 3 billion or more actually contributed. 13

Why the myth persists: Company formation agencies earn their fee at incorporation. The residency outcome is the customer's problem afterwards.

Widely believedWorking online for my US clients from a Vietnamese tourist visa is fine, everyone does it.

Actually: It is prohibited on paper and tolerated in practice, and those are two different risks. Article 8.2 of the 2014 Law on Entry, Exit, Transit and Residence bars foreigners from labour activities on a tourist entry; administrative fines run VND 15–25 million (roughly US$600–1,000). Enforcement against people quietly serving foreign clients has been close to nonexistent. That is a tolerance, not a right, and it can be withdrawn without notice. Decide with open eyes; do not let anyone tell you it is legal. 616

Why the myth persists: Everyone's lived experience is that nothing happened to them. Survivorship bias reads as legal advice.

Widely believedThe US and Vietnam have a tax treaty, so I won't be double taxed.

Actually: A treaty was signed in July 2015 and Vietnam ratified it in 2017, but the US Senate never did, so it has never entered into force. There are no treaty tie-breaker rules for dual residency and no reduced withholding. Your entire defense against double taxation is the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion and the Foreign Tax Credit. 19

Why the myth persists: The treaty was signed with fanfare in 2015 and the announcement articles still rank well. Almost nobody publishes the non-ratification follow-up.

Your pathway, in questions

Answer honestly rather than optimistically. Every answer narrows to exactly one route, including the routes that turn out not to exist. You can go back at any point.

    The pathways in full

    Every legal route, whether or not the tree sent you there. Read your own first, then read the one you would fall back to.

    90-Day E-Visa

    EV low

    Vietnam's default entry permission for Americans: fully online, up to 90 days, available single or multiple entry. This is the tool you will use for scouting trips, and the one most long-stayers quietly live on.

    Best for
    Scouting trips, the gap between arriving and having a work permit approved, and anyone who has not yet triggered a long-term category.
    You get
    Up to 90 days
    Renewable
    Not extended in the ordinary case — you apply for a new one. Practice varies and in-country extension is not something to plan around.
    Work locally
    No. Labour activity on a tourist entry is prohibited under Article 8.2 of the 2014 Law.
    Family
    Each person applies separately, including children.
    Toward permanent residence
    No.
    Realistic timeline
    3 to 5 working days standard. Apply at least two weeks before departure so you can survive one rejection and reapply.

    Hard requirements

    • US passport valid at least 6 months beyond entry — Count from your intended entry date, not your application date. 8
    • Passport-standard digital photo and a scan of the passport bio page — Plain white background, no glasses, face fully visible. Photo rejection is the most common cause of a failed application. 8
    • A declared port of entry — You must name the checkpoint you will physically use, and it must match on arrival. 8

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    E-visa, single entryUS$25Official government fee. Non-refundable, including when your own typo causes the rejection. 8
    E-visa, multiple entryUS$50Worth it for anyone who will leave and return within the 90 days. 8

    Step by step

    1. Apply on the official government portal only

      Vietnam's national e-visa portal is a government site. Dozens of commercial sites clone its look and charge US$50 to 90 for the same US$25 application. Confirm you are on a .gov.vn domain before you pay. 8

      Who: You Takes: 30 minutes

    2. Enter your name exactly as machine-readable on your passport

      Surname and given names in the same fields the passport uses. A middle name in the wrong box is a rejection.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Have the passport physically in front of you.

    3. Choose the correct entry port

      If you might fly into Tan Son Nhat but could reroute to Noi Bai, this matters. See the gotcha on port matching.

      Who: You

    4. Pay and save the registration code

      The code is how you retrieve the visa. Without it, recovery is painful.

      Who: You

    5. Download and print the approved e-visa

      Carry a paper copy. Airline check-in staff at US airports frequently ask to see it before boarding, and phone batteries die.

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Applying through a lookalike commercial site

    Consequence: You pay two to four times the official fee, and sometimes get a visa-on-arrival letter you did not want.

    Avoid it: Verify the domain ends in .gov.vn before entering card details.

    Arriving at a different port than declared

    Consequence: Refused entry at the border, with the airline liable to fly you back.

    Avoid it: If your routing changes, apply for a new e-visa with the correct port.

    Treating the 90 days as renewable in-country

    Consequence: Overstay, fines, and a border record that makes every future application harder.

    Avoid it: Book the exit before you enter.

    5-Year Visa Exemption Certificate

    VEC moderate

    The best-value document in Vietnamese immigration, and the least known. For people of Vietnamese origin and the foreign spouses and children of Vietnamese citizens: five years of unlimited entries, up to 180 days per entry, no visa fee each time.

    Best for
    Americans with a Vietnamese parent or grandparent, former Vietnamese nationals, and foreign spouses of Vietnamese citizens who do not need to work locally.
    You get
    5 years, capped at 180 days per single entry. Cannot exceed remaining passport validity.
    Renewable
    Yes, reapply on the same basis.
    Work locally
    No — it is an entry exemption, not a work authorisation. Working still requires a work permit or a documented exemption.
    Family
    Spouse and children apply on the family relationship, each with their own certificate.
    Toward permanent residence
    Not directly, but it coexists with other applications and takes the pressure off completely.
    Realistic timeline
    Typically a few weeks once you hold the proof documents. Finding the proof documents can take months.

    Hard requirements

    • Passport valid at least 1 year — Longer is better; the certificate cannot outlast the passport. 12
    • Proof of Vietnamese origin, or proof of family relationship to a Vietnamese citizen — For Viet Kieu: a decision permitting relinquishment of Vietnamese nationality, a certificate of loss of nationality, an old Vietnamese ID card (even expired), a household registration book, or a birth records extract. For spouses and children: marriage or birth certificate plus the Vietnamese relative's identity documents. 12

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Certificate feeRoughly US$10 to 25Set by the issuing mission. Confirm with the embassy or consulate handling your application. 12
    Document retrieval from Vietnamese archivesHighly variableFor Viet Kieu whose family left decades ago, finding the proof is the whole cost of this pathway. Budget time, not just money.

    Step by step

    1. Establish which proof of origin you can actually obtain

      Work backwards from what exists: a parent's Vietnamese birth certificate, an old household registration book, a relinquishment-of-nationality decision. Ask the oldest relative in the family first — this is where the documents usually are.

      Who: You and your family Takes: Weeks to months

      Blocked by: Everything downstream waits on this.

    2. Get foreign-issued documents apostilled

      US marriage and birth certificates used as proof need authentication. From 11 September 2026 this is an apostille rather than consular legalization — see the gotcha, the timing matters right now. 7

      Who: You

    3. Have documents translated into Vietnamese and notarised

      Use a translation office that routinely serves immigration filings.

      Who: You

    4. File with the Vietnamese embassy or consulate, or with Immigration inside Vietnam

      US-based applicants normally file with the Embassy in Washington DC or the Consulate General in San Francisco or Houston.

      Who: You Where: Vietnamese diplomatic mission, or Vietnam Immigration Department

    5. Collect the certificate and check every field

      Verify the name spelling and validity dates before you leave the counter. Corrections later are a new application.

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Assuming you do not qualify because you were born in the US and speak no Vietnamese

    Consequence: You spend US$10,000 on a company you did not need.

    Avoid it: Vietnamese origin runs through ancestry and former nationality, not language or birthplace. Check before you dismiss it.

    Letting the certificate outrun the passport

    Consequence: The certificate is issued short, or invalidated when you renew the passport.

    Avoid it: Renew the US passport first if it has under two years left.

    Treating 180 days per entry as 180 days per year

    Consequence: Overstay.

    Avoid it: The clock resets on each entry, but each stay is capped. Track entry dates.

    TT Family Visa and 3-Year Residence Card

    TT moderate

    The residence route for foreign spouses, children, and parents of Vietnamese citizens. Produces a temporary residence card valid up to 3 years, which functions as a multiple-entry visa substitute.

    Best for
    Americans married to Vietnamese citizens who want a stable base rather than a rolling permission.
    You get
    TT residence card up to 3 years
    Renewable
    Yes, on continuing relationship and valid passport.
    Work locally
    The card itself is not work authorisation. However, being married to a Vietnamese citizen and residing in Vietnam has historically been one of the work permit exemption categories. Confirm your status under Decree 219/2025 with your employer or a licensed adviser before you start work — do not assume it carried over unchanged.
    Family
    Children of the marriage are covered on the same family basis.
    Toward permanent residence
    Permanent residence exists for spouses of Vietnamese citizens after a qualifying period of continuous temporary residence. Treat it as a long-horizon goal and take specific legal advice — the qualifying rules are strict and periodically amended.
    Realistic timeline
    Plan 2 to 4 months from starting document collection to card in hand. Card processing itself is 5 to 10 working days once filed.

    Hard requirements

    • Marriage registered and recognised in Vietnam — A marriage performed abroad must be recorded in Vietnam, or evidenced by a legalised or apostilled consular note of the registration. 11
    • Passport with at least 13 months validity — The card must expire at least 30 days before the passport does, so short passports produce short cards. 1110
    • Entry on a visa consistent with family purpose — You generally need to be in Vietnam on a TT visa, sponsored by your Vietnamese spouse, before the card application. Entering on an e-visa and converting is not reliable. 11
    • Vietnamese spouse's identity and residence documents — Certified copies of the national ID or citizen identity card and household registration. 11

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Temporary residence cardRoughly US$145 to 320 depending on validityRenewals and extensions are far cheaper, around US$10. Confirm current fees at filing. 10
    Apostille or legalization plus certified translationUS$150 to 500Depends on how many US documents you need and which state issued them.
    Agency assistance, optionalUS$300 to 800Genuinely optional on this route if your Vietnamese spouse can attend the offices with you.

    Step by step

    1. Register or record the marriage so Vietnam recognises it

      If you married in the US, this is the step that gates everything else. Get the marriage certificate apostilled, translated, and recorded. 11

      Who: You and your spouse Takes: Weeks

      Blocked by: Nothing else can proceed until the marriage is documented Vietnamese-side.

    2. Your Vietnamese spouse sponsors your TT visa

      The sponsorship is filed by the Vietnamese citizen, not by you.

      Who: Your Vietnamese spouse Where: Vietnam Immigration Department

    3. Enter Vietnam on the TT visa

      Enter on the family-purpose visa, not on an e-visa, so the residence card application is consistent.

      Who: You

    4. Complete temporary residence declaration at your address

      Within 12 hours of arriving at the accommodation. Your landlord or spouse files it. See the gotcha — this trips up more people than any other single rule. 22

      Who: Landlord or host Takes: Same day

    5. File the residence card application

      Form, photos at 3x4cm on white background taken within 6 months, passport, marriage and family documents, spouse's ID and household registration. 11

      Who: You, with your spouse Where: Provincial Immigration Department Takes: 5 to 10 working days

    How this goes wrong

    Relying on a US marriage certificate that was never recorded in Vietnam

    Consequence: Application refused; months lost.

    Avoid it: Record the marriage first, then everything else.

    Applying with a passport that has under 13 months left

    Consequence: You get a short card or a refusal, and pay again next year.

    Avoid it: Renew the passport before you file.

    Starting work on the strength of the card alone

    Consequence: Illegal employment exposure for you and your employer.

    Avoid it: Get the work permit, or get the exemption confirmed in writing under Decree 219/2025.

    Work Permit, LĐ Visa, and 2-Year Residence Card

    LĐ1 LĐ2 moderate

    The main road. Your employer obtains a work permit under Decree 219/2025, which supports an LĐ visa and then a temporary residence card aligned to the permit. Decree 219 made this materially faster than it was before August 2025.

    Best for
    Anyone with a genuine Vietnamese employer, including local subsidiaries of American companies, schools, and universities.
    You get
    Work permit up to 2 years; residence card aligned to it and capped at 2 years.
    Renewable
    Yes. Start renewal well before expiry — the card cannot outlast the permit.
    Work locally
    Yes, for the sponsoring employer, in the position named on the permit. The permit is job-specific and employer-specific.
    Family
    Yes — spouse and children under 18 on TT dependant status, sponsored by you once you hold the card.
    Toward permanent residence
    Not directly, but continuous lawful residence is the foundation for any later permanent residence application.
    Realistic timeline
    Under Decree 219/2025, the work permit itself is a single 10-working-day process, replacing the old two-stage sequence of job position approval plus permit. Realistically, 8 to 14 weeks door to door, because document authentication in the US dominates the schedule.

    Hard requirements

    • A Vietnamese legal entity willing to sponsor — The entity files in its own name. No entity, no permit. 3
    • Expert test: degree or equivalent plus 2 years relevant experience — Reduced to 1 year for priority sectors — science, technology, innovation, and national digital transformation. Down from 3 years under the old Decree 152/2020 regime. 34
    • Criminal record check issued within the last 6 months — For Americans this is normally the FBI Identity History Summary. The 6-month clock is the single most common sequencing failure on this pathway. 3
    • Health certificate — Issued by a hospital recognised for this purpose. In practice, done in Vietnam after arrival, at a licensed international or provincial hospital. 3
    • Authenticated degree and professional certificates — US-issued diplomas must be authenticated and translated. From 11 September 2026, apostille replaces consular legalization for documents from the US. 37

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Work permit state feeRoughly US$25 to 50 equivalentSet at provincial level and varies. Usually paid by the employer. 3
    FBI Identity History Summary plus channelerUS$18 government fee, US$50 to 100 via an approved channelerThe channeler is worth it — turnaround drops from weeks to days.
    Apostille on degree and criminal recordUS$20 to 200 depending on issuing authority and expeditingFederal documents such as the FBI summary are apostilled by the US Department of State; state-issued documents by that state's Secretary of State.
    Certified Vietnamese translationUS$100 to 300
    Temporary residence cardRoughly US$145 to 320 10
    Immigration law firm, optionalUS$800 to 2,500Most employers with foreign staff already have a firm and absorb this.

    Step by step

    1. Secure the offer and confirm the entity can sponsor

      Ask directly whether the hiring entity holds a Vietnamese business registration certificate and has filed work permits before.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Everything depends on this.

    2. Order the FBI Identity History Summary — but time it deliberately

      It must be less than 6 months old when the application is filed. Ordering it too early is as damaging as ordering it too late. Work backwards from your employer's filing date. 3

      Who: You Takes: Days via an approved channeler

    3. Authenticate your degree and criminal record

      From 11 September 2026, obtain an apostille rather than going through Vietnamese consular legalization. Federal documents go to the US Department of State; state-issued documents to the relevant Secretary of State. 7

      Who: You Takes: 1 to 6 weeks depending on state and expediting

    4. Send authenticated documents to your employer for translation and filing

      Your employer submits the work permit application under Decree 219/2025. 3

      Who: Your employer Takes: 10 working days

    5. Enter Vietnam and complete the health certificate

      Done at a licensed hospital in Vietnam. Straightforward, half a day.

      Who: You Where: Licensed hospital in Vietnam

    6. Temporary residence declaration within 12 hours of reaching your accommodation

      Filed by your landlord or hotel. Confirm it was actually done. 22

      Who: Landlord or employer

    7. Convert to the LĐ visa and apply for the residence card

      The card is aligned to the work permit and must expire at least 30 days before your passport. 10

      Who: Employer, with you Takes: 5 to 10 working days

    How this goes wrong

    Getting the FBI check apostilled 7 months before the employer files

    Consequence: Rejected on document age. You reorder and re-authenticate, losing 4 to 6 weeks.

    Avoid it: Agree the filing date with your employer, then work backwards.

    Assuming the permit transfers when you change jobs

    Consequence: You are working illegally from your first day at the new employer.

    Avoid it: The permit is employer-specific. A new employer files a new permit.

    Letting the residence card lapse while the permit is renewed

    Consequence: A gap in lawful residence, which complicates every future application.

    Avoid it: Start renewal 60 days out. Do not wait for the employer to remember.

    Passport with under 2 years left

    Consequence: Card issued short, so you repeat the whole exercise early.

    Avoid it: Renew the passport in the US before you move.

    Work Permit Exemption Confirmation

    LĐ1 moderate

    Not everyone who works in Vietnam needs a work permit. Decree 219/2025 sets out roughly 15 to 20 exemption categories, and an exemption still requires a written confirmation from the labour authority. Skipping the confirmation because you 'are exempt' is itself a violation.

    Best for
    Intra-company transferees, company owners and board members above capital thresholds, short assignments under 90 days in a calendar year, and spouses of Vietnamese citizens residing in Vietnam.
    You get
    Confirmation up to 2 years, supporting a residence card of matching length.
    Renewable
    Yes, on the same basis.
    Work locally
    Yes, within the scope of the exemption category and the entity named on it.
    Family
    Yes, dependants on TT status once you hold a residence card.
    Toward permanent residence
    No direct route.
    Realistic timeline
    Shorter than a full work permit, but do not assume it is instant — build in 4 to 8 weeks including document authentication.

    Hard requirements

    • You fall in a listed exemption category — Common ones for Americans: intra-company transfer after 12+ months with the foreign parent that has a commercial presence in Vietnam; owner or capital contributor of an LLC, or board member of a joint stock company, above the applicable capital threshold; total working time under 90 days in a calendar year; married to a Vietnamese citizen and residing in Vietnam. The list is defined by decree and was restated in Decree 219/2025 — have it checked against the current text for your exact facts. 35
    • Written confirmation of exemption obtained before you start work — The exemption is a status you must be granted, not one you can assert. 3

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Confirmation filingNominal state feeUsually handled and paid by the employer.
    Supporting document authenticationUS$150 to 400Same apostille and translation work as the full permit route, generally less of it.

    Step by step

    1. Identify the exact exemption category in the current decree

      Have your employer's counsel name the specific clause. 'We think you're exempt' is not a filing. 3

      Who: Employer's counsel

    2. Assemble evidence for that specific category

      Intra-company transfer needs employment history with the parent; capital-based exemptions need the investment registration and capital contribution evidence.

      Who: You and your employer

    3. File for the written exemption confirmation

      Filed by the employer with the labour authority before work begins.

      Who: Your employer

    4. Use the confirmation to obtain the visa and residence card

      The confirmation plays the same role a work permit would in the residence card application. 10

      Who: Employer, with you

    How this goes wrong

    Working on the assumption of exemption without the confirmation

    Consequence: Illegal employment for you and a fine for the employer, regardless of whether you genuinely qualified.

    Avoid it: No work before the paper exists.

    Relying on the under-90-days exemption repeatedly

    Consequence: Decree 219 frames this as total working time under 90 days in one calendar year, not per trip. Repeat short trips add up.

    Avoid it: Track cumulative days across the calendar year.

    Assuming the pre-August-2025 exemption list still applies

    Consequence: Filing under a repealed decree.

    Avoid it: Decree 219/2025 replaced Decree 152/2020 and its Decree 70/2023 amendments from 7 August 2025.

    UĐ1 Digital Technology Visa

    UĐ1 UĐ2 high

    Vietnam's newest and longest standard visa, live since 1 July 2026 under Law 118/2025/QH15. Up to 5 years for high-quality digital technology personnel, with UĐ2 covering the spouse and children under 18.

    Best for
    Senior software, AI, semiconductor, and digital infrastructure professionals who can attract a Vietnamese institutional sponsor.
    You get
    Up to 5 years — the longest standard validity in the current framework.
    Renewable
    Expected, on continuing sponsorship.
    Work locally
    Yes, within the sponsored role.
    Family
    Yes — that is exactly what UĐ2 is for.
    Toward permanent residence
    Not yet defined. The conversion route from UĐ1 status to a temporary residence card was still awaiting implementing regulations during 2026.
    Realistic timeline
    Unsettled. Treat published timelines with scepticism until implementing regulations and a track record exist.

    Hard requirements

    • Recognised as high-quality personnel in the digital technology industry — The criteria run through an institution: a Vietnamese employer, a university, or a research body. This structurally excludes freelancers and remote employees of foreign companies. 12
    • An institutional sponsor in Vietnam — As with the work permit, no sponsor means no application. 2

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    State feesNot yet settled in published guidanceThis category is new. Verify current fees directly with the Immigration Department or through counsel before budgeting.

    Step by step

    1. Confirm the category is operational for your profile today

      The law took effect 1 July 2026, but detailed implementing regulations were still emerging. Ask the sponsor's counsel what has actually been granted, not what the law permits. 1

      Who: You and your sponsor

    2. Have the sponsoring institution assess you against the high-quality personnel criteria

      This is the gate. It is an institutional judgement, not a self-assessment.

      Who: Your sponsor

    3. Run the standard document authentication in parallel

      Degrees, employment history, and criminal record will be needed on any route. Do this work regardless of which category you end on.

      Who: You

    4. Keep the work permit route open as your fallback

      Until UĐ1 has a visible track record, treat it as an upgrade on a work permit plan, not a replacement for one.

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Reading UĐ1 as a digital nomad visa

    Consequence: Months spent pursuing a category you cannot enter without an institutional sponsor.

    Avoid it: If no Vietnamese institution will name you, this route is closed.

    Abandoning a viable work permit application to wait for UĐ1

    Consequence: You lose a working route for an unproven one.

    Avoid it: Run them in sequence, not instead of each other.

    DT Investor Visa and Residence Card

    DT1 DT2 DT3 DT4 high

    Four tiers keyed to how much capital you actually contribute to a Vietnamese company. The tier determines everything, and only DT3 and above produce a residence card.

    Best for
    People building a real Vietnamese business with meaningful capital. A poor fit for anyone forming a shell company purely to buy residency.
    You get
    DT1: visa up to 5 years, residence card up to 10 years. DT2: up to 5 years, card up to 5. DT3: up to 3 years, card up to 3. DT4: visa up to 12 months, no residence card.
    Renewable
    Yes, while the investment and the company remain in good standing.
    Work locally
    In your own invested company. Note that owners and board members above capital thresholds may also fall in a work permit exemption category.
    Family
    Yes, dependants on TT status once you hold a residence card — which again means DT3 or above.
    Toward permanent residence
    DT1 is the tier most often discussed alongside a long-term permanent residence horizon. Take specific legal advice rather than relying on marketing claims.
    Realistic timeline
    3 to 6 months from decision to residence card, dominated by investment registration and getting capital properly contributed and evidenced.

    Hard requirements

    • DT1: contributed capital of VND 100 billion or more, roughly US$3.8M — Or investment in a sector or area the government specifically encourages. 13
    • DT2: VND 50 to under 100 billion, roughly US$1.9M to 3.8M 13
    • DT3: VND 3 to under 50 billion, roughly US$115k to 1.9M — The entry point for a residence card. Below this you are in DT4 and get no card. 13
    • DT4: under VND 3 billion — Visa up to 12 months, no residence card. Read the reality check before choosing this. 13
    • A real investment registration and actual capital contribution — Registered capital that is never contributed does not hold up. The capital must move and be evidenced. 13

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Company formation and investment registrationUS$1,500 to 5,000 in professional feesBefore any capital contribution.
    The capital itselfVND 3 billion minimum for a residence cardThis is contributed capital in a Vietnamese company, not an escrow deposit you get back.
    Ongoing accounting, audit, and tax complianceUS$2,000 to 8,000 per yearThe cost people forget. A Vietnamese company files monthly and annually whether or not it trades.
    Visa and residence cardRoughly US$145 to 320 for the card 10

    Step by step

    1. Decide the tier before you incorporate

      The capital number drives the visa outcome. Incorporating first and discovering you are in DT4 is the classic and expensive error. 13

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Do this before spending anything.

    2. Obtain the investment registration certificate and enterprise registration certificate

      Two separate documents. Both are needed downstream.

      Who: Your Vietnamese counsel Takes: 4 to 8 weeks

    3. Open the direct investment capital account and actually transfer the capital

      Capital must come in through the correct account type or it will not be recognised as contributed. Get this wrong and the money is in Vietnam but not counted.

      Who: You, with your bank and counsel

      Blocked by: The visa application depends on evidenced contribution.

    4. Apply for the DT visa at the tier your contribution supports

      The tier is assessed on what you actually contributed.

      Who: Your company sponsors you

    5. Apply for the residence card if you are at DT3 or above

      Same 5 to 10 working day processing as other card types. 10

      Who: You

    How this goes wrong

    Registering large capital but contributing little

    Consequence: Tier assessed on the contribution, not the registration. You paid for a company and got a 12-month visa.

    Avoid it: Only register capital you will genuinely transfer, and transfer it through the correct account.

    Ignoring ongoing compliance cost

    Consequence: A dormant company accrues filing obligations and penalties, and a struck-off company takes your visa basis with it.

    Avoid it: Budget annual compliance from day one.

    Believing an agency that says VND 3 billion is not really required

    Consequence: DT4, no card, and no refund.

    Avoid it: The tier boundaries are published. Ask the agency to point at the decree.

    DH Student Visa

    DH low

    Sponsored by the institution that admitted you. A legitimate, low-cost way to hold lawful long-term status while you build the Vietnamese language ability and network that make the other routes viable.

    Best for
    Younger movers, career changers, and anyone treating a first year in Vietnam as an investment in optionality.
    You get
    Aligned to the program, typically up to 1 year at a time, with a residence card possible for longer programs.
    Renewable
    Yes, while enrolled and progressing.
    Work locally
    No. Student status is not work authorisation, and the tourist-visa reasoning about remote work applies here too.
    Family
    Limited. Do not plan a family move around this route.
    Toward permanent residence
    No, but it builds continuous lawful residence and local credentials.
    Realistic timeline
    6 to 12 weeks from admission to visa in hand.

    Hard requirements

    • Admission to an institution licensed to host foreign students — Universities and accredited full-time language programs. A part-time evening class at a private centre generally cannot sponsor you.
    • Proof of funds and accommodation — Requirements are set by the institution and vary widely.
    • Authenticated prior academic records — Same apostille and translation pipeline as the work permit route. 7

    What it costs

    ItemAmountNote
    Tuition, full-time Vietnamese language programUS$1,000 to 3,000 per yearUniversity degree programs cost more; still well below US equivalents.
    Visa and residence cardUS$145 to 320 for a card, less for visa-only status 10

    Step by step

    1. Secure admission from a licensed institution

      Confirm in writing that they sponsor DH visas for foreign students, and ask how many they issued last year.

      Who: You

      Blocked by: Nothing proceeds without the admission letter.

    2. Authenticate prior academic records

      Apostille and certified translation. 7

      Who: You

    3. The institution sponsors the visa

      Filed by the school, not by you.

      Who: Your institution

    4. Enter, declare temporary residence, and apply for the card if the program supports one

      Standard 12-hour accommodation declaration on arrival. 22

      Who: You and your landlord

    How this goes wrong

    Enrolling at a private language centre that cannot sponsor

    Consequence: You paid tuition and got no status.

    Avoid it: Confirm sponsorship capability in writing before paying.

    Taking paid work on student status

    Consequence: Same illegal employment exposure as the tourist visa case.

    Avoid it: Keep income sources outside Vietnam, or convert to a work permit.

    Ten traps

    Cross-cutting failures that belong to no single pathway. If you read only one section of this guide, read this one.

    1The apostille switchover lands on 11 September 2026

    expensive

    The trap. Vietnam acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention on 31 December 2025, and it enters into force for Vietnam on 11 September 2026. Documents authenticated the old way and the new way are both in circulation right now, and agencies are giving out instructions written for the old regime. Getting consular legalization when an apostille is required, or the reverse, wastes 4 to 8 weeks and non-refundable fees.

    Do this instead. For US public documents intended for use in Vietnam from 11 September 2026 onward, obtain a single apostille: US Department of State for federal documents such as the FBI Identity History Summary, and the relevant Secretary of State for state-issued documents like degrees and marriage certificates. Before you order anything, confirm with the specific Vietnamese authority that will receive the document which form they are accepting that week. Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs — the Consular Department in Hanoi and the Department of Foreign Affairs in Ho Chi Minh City — issues apostilles on the Vietnamese side. 7

    Tied to a rule change — re-check this after March 11, 2027.

    2The FBI criminal record check has a 6-month shelf life

    expensive

    The trap. Work permit applications require a criminal record check issued within the last 6 months. Applicants order it as their very first task, then spend four months on job offers and degree authentication, and file with a document that is five and a half months old — or already expired.

    Do this instead. Fix the employer's filing date first. Order the FBI Identity History Summary through an approved channeler roughly 6 to 8 weeks before that date, then apostille it immediately. 3

    3Your e-visa names one port of entry and means it

    trip ending

    The trap. The e-visa carries a declared checkpoint. Arrive at a different airport or land border and you can be refused entry, with the airline liable for flying you back.

    Do this instead. Match the port to your actual ticket. If your routing changes — a rebooking through Hanoi instead of Ho Chi Minh City — apply for a new e-visa before you fly. US$25 is cheaper than a denied boarding. 8

    4Your residence card must expire at least 30 days before your passport

    expensive

    The trap. People with 18 months left on a US passport apply for a 2-year residence card and receive a card truncated to about 17 months, then pay the full fee again the following year.

    Do this instead. Renew the US passport before applying for or renewing any Vietnamese residence card. Treat 2 years of remaining passport validity as your floor. 10

    5Somebody must declare your address to the police within 12 hours

    annoying

    The trap. The obligation sits with the accommodation provider, so foreigners assume it is handled. Hotels do it automatically. Private landlords and friends whose spare room you are using very often do not. The declaration is free, uses form NA17, and its absence surfaces months later as a problem in a residence card application.

    Do this instead. Ask the landlord directly, in the first 12 hours, whether the declaration has been filed, and ask for confirmation. Repeat at every address change. Non-compliance exposes the host to fines in the millions of VND. 22

    6The 183-day line makes you taxable on worldwide income

    expensive

    The trap. Presence for 183 days in a calendar year, or across 12 consecutive months from first arrival, makes you a Vietnamese tax resident on worldwide income at rates up to 35%. A habitual residence — a registered address or a fixed-term lease — can also make you resident. Americans arriving in August often assume the first partial year is free. The rolling 12-month test says otherwise.

    Do this instead. Count days from your first entry stamp, and get advice before your first 183rd day, not after. With no US-Vietnam treaty in force, there are no tie-breaker rules to rescue a dual-residency position. 1719

    7Under VND 3 billion, the investor route gives you no residence card

    expensive

    The trap. DT4 — capital under VND 3 billion — grants a visa of up to 12 months and no temporary residence card. Formation agencies quote the incorporation fee, not the residency outcome.

    Do this instead. If residency is the goal, the number to clear is VND 3 billion in genuinely contributed capital, entering at DT3. If you cannot clear it, solve residence a different way and decide on the company purely as a business question. 13

    8Nobody can sell you a Vietnamese golden visa

    expensive

    The trap. A 5-to-10-year golden visa was proposed in 2025 and has been reported worldwide as though it launched. As of this guide's verification date there is no decree and no application channel. Some sites cite a 'Resolution 41/2026/QH15' that no government source confirms.

    Do this instead. If anyone offers to process a Vietnamese golden visa, ask for the decree number and the government portal. There is no correct answer they can give. Use the DT tiers or UĐ1 instead, both of which actually exist. 14

    9Your work permit belongs to your employer, not to you

    trip ending

    The trap. The permit names one employer and one position. Changing jobs does not carry it across, and the residence card built on it falls with it.

    Do this instead. Before accepting a new offer, confirm the new employer will file a fresh permit and understand the gap in between. Never resign before the new filing is in motion. 3

    10A car licence does not convert into a motorbike licence

    trip ending

    The trap. Conversion produces a Vietnamese licence of the same class as the US original. Most Americans hold car-only licences, then ride a motorbike anyway. After an accident, insurers decline on the licence class, and motorbike injuries are the largest single health risk to foreigners in Vietnam.

    Do this instead. If you intend to ride, obtain the motorbike category properly rather than assuming your car licence converts. Confirm your health and travel policies cover motorbike use at your licence class, in writing. 23

    The move itself, phase by phase

    Eight phases, in order. These apply whichever pathway you took; items marked with a pathway only appear for that route. Your ticks are saved in this browser.

    DecideDocumentsLeave United StatesMoneyArrivalFirst 90 daysOngoingContingency

    Decide and pressure-test

    T-180 to T-120 days

    Before you spend a dollar. The goal of this phase is to kill bad plans cheaply.

    Assemble and authenticate documents

    T-150 to T-60 days

    This phase, not the visa application, is what actually determines your timeline. US document authentication is slow, sequential, and unforgiving.

    Close out the United States

    T-90 to T-0 days

    The US side of the move. Being a US citizen abroad is an ongoing legal relationship, not a departure.

    Money and banking

    T-60 to T+30 days

    Vietnam is substantially a cash economy in daily life and a heavily documented one in official life. Both facts matter.

    Arrival week

    T-0 to T+7 days

    A short list, but one item on it has a 12-hour deadline.

    First 90 days

    T+7 to T+90 days

    Converting arrival into residence. Most of this runs in parallel; start all of it in week two.

    Staying legal, year after year

    Continuous

    Vietnamese status is a renewal treadmill. Build a calendar in your first month and never rely on an employer to remember for you.

    Contingency and exit

    Have this before you need it

    Written while things are going well, so that it exists when they are not.
